page: Microsoft Azure D2als_v7 is an entry-level, compute-leaning virtual machine within the general-purpose Dals_v7 family. Powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance exposes two vCPUs across a single physical core via multithreading. It includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a dedicated 32 MB L3 cache slice. System memory is sized at 4.0 GB (2.0 GB per vCPU), and the instance provision includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring reliance on external Azure network storage volumes. Hardware acceleration flags include extensive instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and hardware AES/SHA encryption accelerators.

Benchmark measurements highlight exceptional single-thread execution speed paired with standard entry-tier aggregate limits. In single-core testing, the AMD core achieves top-decile results, scoring 2,771 on Geekbench single-core, 38.86 GB/s in single-threaded gzip compression, and 17.14 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance operates on a single physical core with two execution threads, multi-threaded metrics remain modest: Geekbench multi-core registers at 3,570 and PassMark CPU overall scores 4,813, ranking in the lower quartile. Potentially uncached main memory bandwidth reaches 43.43 GB/s read and 32.92 GB/s write throughput.

Cost efficiency is strongly optimized for lightweight, latency-sensitive single-core operations where high clock frequencies provide an advantage without the expense of larger memory allocations. With only 4.0 GB of RAM and absence of local scratch disks, it is not suited for memory-intensive caches or large dataset processing. Microsoft Azure D2als_v7 functions effectively for microservices, lightweight web request handling, software builds with low parallelism requirements, automated scripting, and utility orchestration jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D2als_v7 is an x86_64 instance from the Dals_v7 family providing 2 vCPUs on a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 physical core running at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it provides 4.0 GB of memory and includes no local ephemeral storage. Hardware vector support is broad, including AVX-512 and VNNI instructions. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-threaded compute efficiency, yielding a 2,771 Geekbench single-core score and rapid single-stream compression performance. Multi-threaded throughput is restricted by the single-core footprint, scoring 3,570 in multi-core Geekbench. Lacking local disks and high memory density, this instance delivers strong cost efficiency for lightweight workloads, background services, build tasks with modest resource footprints, and general low-memory orchestration.
